Subject: Midpoint trajectory steer: program-level asks ahead of QBR

Team —

Quick mid-quarter check. QBR is two weeks out; before we lock the narrative I want us to be explicit about where we need leadership-level steering and what we expect to escalate to the exec forum. Summary below (short bullets, followed by asks).

Status highlights (top-line):
- Hosting latency program: 6% better than plan on tail latency but cost per token up 8% due to current batch sizing on peak windows.
- Dedicated onboarding: two pilot customers (Helix + Lumen) in pilot; Helix integration delayed by pending security evidence.
- Redwood Optimize rollout: on track for beta, but we hit a validation issue on quantization regressions for long-context tests.

Program-level asks (what I want from you):
1) Scope steer: decide whether we re-scope the full latency initiative to prioritize cost optimization (quantization + batching) versus feature completeness (streaming tool-calls). I need the decision by Fri 11/13 to adjust roadmap for QBR.
2) Resource reassign: request +0.5 FTE infra sdr from Platform for three sprints to get batching experiments into production.
3) Procurement / Security unblock: ask CS to push Helix security questionnaire to completion and confirm data residency controls; without this, Dedicated sign-off slips.

Attachments: I attached a working QBR deck and a dependency matrix with owners and ETA columns. Please review the matrix and flag any reassigns inline.

Next steps: Markus — can you call out the cost vs feature tradeoff recommendation? Laura — can you confirm whether Platform can spare the infra resource for three sprints and who the fallback is?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Go-to-Market Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-11-22_QBR-draft-v3.pptx (pptx), dependency_matrix_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.inference>

Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Midpoint trajectory steer: program-level asks ahead of QBR

Vanessa — thanks for the concise breakdown. A couple quick thoughts:

1) Cost vs feature: given the current runway and the fact that cost delta is already visible in customer telemetry, my recommendation is to prioritize the cost optimization path (quant + batching) for the next two releases, and defer non-essential streaming enhancements to post-QBR. We should quantify estimated savings (savings target: 12% unit cost reduction) in the deck.

2) Infra resource: I can free the +0.5 FTE for three sprints, but that will push two lower-priority infra tickets to the backlog (see ticket list in the dependency matrix). If Laura is OK with that, I'll reassign starting 11/16.

3) Helix security: we need a clear owner on the evidence collection. CS has done the initial work but it needs Platform/InfoSec sign-off. If we don't have sign-off by 11/18, we should schedule an exec-level bridge.

I'll update slide 4 with the cost projection and a recommended tradeoff statement for the QBR.

—Markus
Director, Product Ops
